title: W3C Web Real-Time Communications Working Group-relevant MDN issues
description: Issue filed on MDN Web Docs related to pages attached to technologies developed by W3C Web Real-Time Communications Working Group

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Another non-number constraint is the deviceId constraint. If you have a deviceId from mediaDevices.enumerateDevices(), you can use it to request a specific device:

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

getUserMedia({
video: {
deviceId: myPreferredCameraDeviceId,
},
});

Chromium based browsers no longer use the ideal (or unspecificied) deviceId video constraint, you can only select 'exact' deviceId as the preferred camera will be ignored in favor of whichever camera was selected in the preferences section..

What did you expect to see?

An indication that ideal (or unspecified) deviceId requests are no longer honored

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

See: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/438606278

Marked as 'wont fix'

Do you have anything more you want to share?

No response

Value

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

This value is null if negotiation has not completed.

What did you expect to see?

This value should be set to the MID of the "m=" section when a local or remote description is applyed, according to RFC 8829 that is referenced by WebRTC specification.

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getDisplayMedia

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

systemAudio

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

systemAudio constraint is misleading. Especially on Chrome or Chromium browsers, where window.speechSynthesisSpeak() called on the same Tab is not captured by navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia() using any constraints - because audio output as a result of a call to window.speechSynthesis.speak() really is output at the system level, not on the current Tab, or any browser Tab.

What did you expect to see?

A note notifying users that Chrome and Chromium browsers on Linux do not capture system audio.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

  • GoogleChrome/developer.chrome.com#3947 (comment)
  • GoogleChrome/developer.chrome.com#3957
  • https://github.com/edisionnano/Screenshare-with-audio-on-Discord-with-Linux#enter-chromium
  • https://github.com/guest271314/captureSystemAudio#references

Do you have anything more you want to share?

In spite of the specification using the terminology "systemAudio" Chromium and Chromium browser authors refuse https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=931749 to support capture of system audio on Linux. Thus the constraint is misleading for user on Linux using Chrome or Chromium.
